text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- State security court determines from mobile phone records that late fugitive mobster Abdullah Catli, whose death in a car accident revealed links between the state and underworld gangs, had carried out many telephone conversations with politicians.
- Iraqi Kurdish leader Jalal Talabani gives assurances that Turkish Kurd rebels will be expelled from northern Iraq when the region's new Kurdish administration is formed.
- Ten youngsters aged between 19 and 25 sentenced to a total of 76 years in jail on dubious charges of being left-wing militants while countless underworld gangs go free.
- The Turkish government is planning to reduce public institutions' debts to each other by making the treasury liable -- a step opposed by economists.
- Former interior minister Mehmet Agar confesses to a parliamentry commission that he gave gangster Catli a false passport and gun license.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktas and Turkish President Suleyman Demirel are due to make a joint declaration that forsees a new Turkish military base in Turkish Cyprus.
- State minister Ufuk Soylemez says this month's privatisation income will be more than the last year's total
- The Turkish armed forces plan to invest $4.5 billion in a scheme that will allow home production of tanks.
